chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Qaṣīr narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:

Whoever takes from his nails and mustache every Jumuʿah and says when taking it: ‘Bismillāh, wa billāh, wa ʿalā sunnati Muḥammad wa Āli Muḥammad, ṣalawātu Allāhi ʿalayhim,’ no clipping of nail nor any trimming will fall from him except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him thereby the freeing of a soul, and he will not fall ill except the illness in which he dies.

key_terms.أَظْفَارِهِ: his nails, referring to the nails being trimmed
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: In the Name of Allah, the opening invocation to be recited
key_terms.جُزَازَةٌ: a trimming or cut portion, here referring to clipped hair
key_terms.جُمُعَةٍ: Friday, the weekly sacred day on which this act is recommended
key_terms.سُنَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the prophetic way of Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad
key_terms.شَارِبِهِ: his mustache, referring to grooming facial hair
key_terms.عِتْقَ نَسَمَةٍ: the freeing of a human soul, used here as a measure of reward

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for trimming the nails and mustache on Jumuʿah with the prescribed dhikr?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of trimming the nails and mustache on Jumuʿah while reciting a prescribed formula invoking Allah and the sunnah of Muḥammad and Āl Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It emphasizes both bodily cleanliness and spiritual reward, promising immense merit and protection from illness until one's final sickness.
